definitions.title: Implicit Differentiation Technique
definitions.latex: \frac{d}{dx}[F(x, y)] = 0 \implies \text{apply chain rule with } \frac{d}{dx}[g(y)] = g'(y)\frac{dy}{dx}, \text{ then solve for } \frac{dy}{dx}
definitions.statement: When an equation F(x, y) = 0 defines y implicitly as a differentiable function of x, differentiate both sides with respect to x treating y as a function of x, then isolate dy/dx algebraically.
conditions: Equation defines y as a locally differentiable function of x
Denominator in dy/dx expression is non-zero
definitions.explanation: Avoids having to solve explicitly for y, which is often difficult or impossible.
definitions.keyTakeaway: Every time you differentiate a term with y with respect to x, append dy/dx.
